actions.findings: Causal-guided knowledge editing allows for targeted modification of unstructured foundational knowledge, addressing the limitations of rigid structured-data editing. [source-b7a6fe44441044d1] [source-0e7e362cf3a94ae3]
actions.limitations: Reliability of automated causal graph extraction remains the primary bottleneck; incorrect causal mapping can introduce systemic errors during premise editing. Empirical validation on specific high-stakes industrial ontologies is missing.

actions.summary: Causal-guided adaptive knowledge editing (CAKE) provides a mechanism for localizing and adjusting foundational premises in LLMs. By mapping causal dependencies, agents can potentially prune or refine erroneous axioms that propagate through reasoning chains. This methodology is particularly relevant for addressing foundational assumptions that are not explicitly defined but implicitly govern agent behavior.
actions.title: Causal-Guided Adaptive Editing for Foundational Assumptions

actions.limitations: Dependency on existing RCA narrative datasets limits applicability in novel or undocumented industrial environments.
actions.next_questions: Can CAKE be used to specialize CRASH agents for specific industrial incident modes?

actions.summary: Reasoning blind spots often arise from implicit, unchecked assumptions embedded in model training. By leveraging causal editing, we can isolate the specific reasoning nodes that lead to circular or biased logic. This framework aids in attribution but does not automatically remediate all classes of meta-reasoning failure.

proposal.summary: Current research cycle focuses on refining the integration of causal-guided knowledge editing (CAKE) into autonomous safety and reasoning frameworks. We have prioritized three projects: challenging foundational assumptions in reasoning, adapting CRASH agent architectures for industrial safety, and identifying metacognitive blind spots in agent workflows. Synthesis is ongoing to ensure these edits maintain epistemic integrity.
